$comment: AMH adapter for Claude Code — wiring only, no logic. All behaviour lives in the constitution and scripts/. Layers this adapter provides: the instructive pre-execution command guard (scripts/command-guard.sh, which reads the PreToolUse payload on stdin — no flag), static deny rails, pre-allowed verification commands, and the comment-budget block cap as a PostToolUse hook. It does NOT provide output redaction: Claude Code has no output-filter hook, so scripts/redact.sh stays available for manual piping and is what the ladder's secret scan and scripts/guards/staged-secrets.sh use. The SessionStart hook translates Claude Code's own CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true into the neutral AAB_REMOTE=1 that amh.conf names — vendor env vars are the adapter's job, never the shipped scripts'. The owner mirrors the hardest rails server-side (branch protection, secret-scanning push protection); these rules bind only agents that load them.
$comment_pythonedit: The second PreToolUse hook is a REPO-LOCAL advisory (DB-062), not part of the shipped rail: scripts/command-guard.sh is integrity-hashed and immutable, so a local pre-execution rule is added beside it rather than inside it. It blocks the first inline-Python file edit per marker lifetime — once per container in practice, the marker being in /tmp with no session component (DB-063) — and passes every later one, mirroring the shipped guard's own .env and destructive advisories — the owner's objection is that an interpreter heredoc is opaque while it runs when Write/Edit would show a diff, and one block is enough to make that a choice rather than a reflex. Hooks in this array are independent: exit 2 from either blocks, so this one cannot weaken the shipped guard. Its ladder rung runs its matcher fixtures; nothing inside the repo can verify the hook still FIRES, only a real command shows that.
$comment_posttooluse: The PostToolUse hook is SALIENCE, not coverage. scripts/guards/comment-budget.sh is a ladder guard and the ladder is what actually gates the tree; running its block cap here as well means a 13-line comment block is reported on the edit that writes it rather than in a ladder run at the end of the session, by which point the prose is written and rewriting it is rework. It cannot block — PostToolUse fires after the tool has run — and it exits 2 because that is the one exit code for which Claude Code feeds a hook's stderr back to the model. It stays silent when it cannot parse its payload or the path is not .kt: a hook that fires spuriously on every edit is one the next session deletes. Nothing can verify from inside the repo that this hook still fires; only a real edit shows that.

hooks.command: bash -c 'if [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE" = true ]; then export AAB_REMOTE=1; fi; exec "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/session-start.sh"'
